items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: Howard McGhee... We made his second outing. And that's where I made what I later on found out to be a classic recording, 'Up In Dodo's Room,' with Howard McGhee's band.

ctx.x: From the Paradise Theatre, yeah. And they had a great, great band in there, a really good band, like some of the top players in the band... He really had started out the club with Kelly Martin, a fine drummer, and he had guys like Howard McGhee and a lot of great players who were in that band. But by the time I got there Howard was gone, but we knew about each other. Big Nick told me one night, he says, "Look, man," he says...

items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: So he asked me, he said, 'Why don't you come on and hook up with me... So I said, 'Well, that's a good idea.' ... Howard formed this band to go into the Finale Club... I'm on the tenor.

ctx.x: Hawkins. They had a great group. They had Sir Charles Thompson on piano, and Oscar Pettiford playing the bass, and Denzil Best on drums. And they came to work at Billy Berg's. So Howard decided to stay here when the band finished the engagement. So he was searching around, trying to find a tenor saxophone player that he liked, and he couldn't find anybody he liked. So he asked me, he said, "Why don't you come on and hook up with me, and switch the tenor?" And I had never thought about playing tenor saxophone...…

I went for it because I knew that he was in the vein closer to what I really wanted to be into. It was like another milestone in my career, because I had to learn all of his library, and making the transition from the alto to the tenor. Because your ear doesn't hear the same on alto and the tenor, unless you're playing them both -- then you can hear them both. But your ear is used to hearing the notes in a certain position, a fourth away, and it takes a little time to get used to hearing it.

items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: I had Red Callender and Teddy Edwards... So anyway, we went down to San Diego

ctx.x: Sonny Criss, Teddy Edwards, Gene Montgomery and Bird. So the bad was beautiful, but we weren't making any money. I mean, people would enjoy it or be loaded, but people would come into the joint that was in there before we'd come in, and we couldn't chase them out and say, "You've got to come back and pay admission." So we played there and it turned out pretty nice. But we wasn't making a lot of money.
You had told me that you wanted to get someone to record that band, and nobody would record it.

items.title: 75230_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: I had Red Callender and Teddy Edwards... So anyway, we went down to San Diego... Sonny Criss, Teddy Edwards, Gene Montgomery and Bird... I would use Wardell and Teddy Edwards if they were here.

ctx.x: Billy Berg's?" I said, "Not particularly, no. I played there. I just come out of there. I've been there eight weeks. Now I'm going down to San Diego. I'm going to play for..." I can't think of the lady's name; "I'm going to play for her."
So I went down to... I had Red Callender and Teddy Edwards...who else did I have...? A cat named Monk played drums, I think. So anyway, we went down to San Diego...
